shared_elements: low-relief carved stone in excavation context
upper register of repeated arch/loop (U-shaped) motifs
small animals perched above the arches
horizontal dividing band filled with hatched/fringed pattern
row of quadruped animals in profile below the band
disc/oval object held or placed near an animal
justification: Both surfaces carry the identical register scheme: a top row of repeated arch/loop motifs with small animals above them, a horizontal band filled with a hatched fringe running the full width, and beneath it profile quadrupeds accompanied by a sinuous snake-like form and disc-shaped objects, all in the same shallow, rounded low relief on the same buff stone. The chief difference is format and preservation — A is a detached rectangular block photographed whole, while B is the head of an upright pillar continuing downward with additional bird and plant-like carvings — but the shared, quite specific compositional formula outweighs this.
